references.text: Isaiah prophesied about the Lord's servant who gave his back to those who struck him: 'I offered my back to those who beat me' ([ref:Jes 50:6|Isaiah 50:6]). This is a messianic prophecy pointing to the abuse Jesus endured.

Isaiah's prophecy about the suffering servant who was despised, afflicted, and beaten for our transgressions ([ref:Jes 53:3-5|Isaiah 53:3-5]) finds its fulfillment in the mistreatment of Jesus after his arrest.
Matthew's parallel account tells that they spat on Jesus, struck him with their fists, and mocked him ([ref:Matt 26:67-68|Matthew 26:67-68]).
Mark's parallel account describes how some began to spit on Jesus, cover his face, strike him, and say, 'Prophesy!' ([ref:Mark 14:65|Mark 14:65]).
The immediate continuation in Luke tells that they covered his face, struck him, demanded that he prophesy, and mocked him with many other words ([ref:Luk 22:64-65|Luke 22:64-65]).
John reports that a guard struck Jesus on the cheek during the hearing before the high priest ([ref:Joh 18:22-23|John 18:22-23]), confirming the physical abuse.

Jesus himself predicted that he would be handed over to the Gentiles, mocked, mistreated, and spat upon ([ref:Luk 18:32-33|Luke 18:32-33]). The mockery and blows in this passage are a direct fulfillment of his own words.
Micah prophesied: 'With a staff they strike the judge of Israel on the cheek' ([ref:Mi 5:1|Micah 5:1]), a prophecy pointing to the abuse of the Messiah.
The psalmist laments being mocked and scorned by all who see him ([ref:Sal 22:7-8|Psalms 22:7-8]), a prophetic lament that echoes in the mockery Jesus faced.
